readings.title: Capital Offenses and Separation
readings.subtitle: The Call to be Set-Apart
readings.text: [Leviticus 20:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [2] <dq>“Say to the children of Yisra’ěl, ‘Any man of the children of Yisra’ěl, or of the strangers who sojourn in Yisra’ěl, who gives any of his offspring to Moleḵ, shall certainly be put to death. The people of the land shall stone him with stones.</dq> [3] <dq>‘And <dn>I</dn>, <dn>I</dn> shall set <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> face against that man, and shall cut <dn>את</dn> him off from the midst of his people, because he has given of his offspring to Moleḵ, so as to defile <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> set-apart place and to profane <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> set-apart Name.</dq> [4] <dq>‘And if the people of the land at all hide <dn>את</dn> their eyes from the man, as he gives any of his offspring to Moleḵ, and they do not kill <dn>את</dn> him,</dq> [5] <dq>then <dn>I</dn> shall set <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> face against that man and against his clan, and shall cut <dn>את</dn> him off – and <dn>את</dn> all who go whoring after him, even go whoring after Moleḵ – from the midst of their people.</dq> [6] <dq>‘And the being who turns to mediums, and to spiritists, to go whoring after them, <dn>I</dn> shall set <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> face against that being and cut <dn>את</dn> him off from the midst of his people.</dq> [7] <dq>‘And you shall set yourselves apart, and shall be set-apart, for <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>,</dq> [8] <dq>and you shall guard <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> laws and do <dn>את</dn> them. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, who sets you apart.</dq> [9] <dq>‘For everyone who curses <dn>את</dn> his father or <dn>את</dn> his mother shall certainly be put to death – he has cursed his father or his mother, his blood is on him.</dq> [10] <dq>‘And a man who commits adultery with <dn>את</dn> the wife of another man, who commits adultery with <dn>את</dn> the wife of his neighbour: the adulterer and the adulteress shall certainly be put to death.</dq> [11] <dq>‘And a man who lies with <dn>את</dn> the wife of his father has uncovered the nakedness of his father, both of them shall certainly be put to death, their blood is upon them.</dq> [12] <dq>‘And a man who lies with <dn>את</dn> his daughter-in-law: both of them shall certainly be put to death, they have made confusion, their blood is upon them.</dq> [13] <dq>‘And a man who lies with <dn>את</dn> a male as he lies with a woman: both of them have done an abomination, they shall certainly be put to death, their blood is upon them.</dq> [14] <dq>‘And a man who marries <dn>את</dn> a woman and <dn>את</dn> her mother: it is wickedness, they are burned with fire, both <dn>את</dn> he and <dn>את</dn> they, that there be no wickedness in your midst.</dq> [15] <dq>‘And a man who has intercourse with a beast: he shall certainly be put to death, and <dn>את</dn> the beast you kill.</dq> [16] <dq>‘And a woman who approaches any beast and mates with it: you shall kill <dn>את</dn> the woman and <dn>את</dn> the beast, they shall certainly be put to death, their blood is upon them.</dq> [17] <dq>‘And a man who takes <dn>את</dn> his sister, his father’s daughter or his mother’s daughter, and sees <dn>את</dn> her nakedness and she sees <dn>את</dn> his nakedness: is it loving-commitment? And they shall be cut off before the eyes of their people. He has uncovered his sister’s nakedness, he bears his crookedness.</dq> [18] <dq>‘And a man who lies with <dn>את</dn> a woman during her sickness and uncovers <dn>את</dn> her nakedness: he has laid bare <dn>את</dn> her flow, and she has uncovered <dn>את</dn> the flow of her blood, both of them shall be cut off from the midst of their people.</dq> [19] <dq>‘And do not uncover the nakedness of your mother’s sister nor of your father’s sister, for that is laying bare <dn>את</dn> one’s own flesh, they bear their crookedness.</dq> [20] <dq>‘And a man who lies with <dn>את</dn> his uncle’s wife: he has uncovered his uncle’s nakedness, they bear their sin, they die childless.</dq> [21] <dq>‘And a man who takes <dn>את</dn> his brother’s wife: it is uncleanness, he has uncovered his brother’s nakedness, they are childless.</dq> [22] <dq>‘And you shall guard <dn>את</dn> all <dn>My</dn> laws and <dn>את</dn> all <dn>My</dn> right-rulings, and do <dn>את</dn> them, so that the land where <dn>I</dn> am bringing <dn>את</dn> you to dwell does not vomit you out.</dq> [23] <dq>‘And do not walk in the laws of the nation which <dn>I</dn> am driving out before you, for they do <dn>את</dn> all these, and therefore <dn>I</dn> loathed them.</dq> [24] <dq>‘But <dn>I</dn> say to you, “You are going to possess <dn>את</dn> their land, and <dn>I</dn> <dn>Myself</dn> give it to you to possess it, a land flowing with milk and honey.” <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, who has separated <dn>את</dn> you from the peoples.</dq> [25] <dq>‘And you shall make a distinction between clean beasts and unclean, and between unclean birds and clean. And do not make <dn>את</dn> yourselves abominable by beast or by bird, or whatever creeps on the ground, which <dn>I</dn> have separated from you as unclean.</dq> [26] <dq>‘And you shall be set-apart to <dn>Me</dn>, for <dn>I</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> am set-apart, and have separated <dn>את</dn> you from the peoples to be <dn>Mine</dn>.</dq> [27] <dq>‘And a man or a woman in whom there is a medium, or who are spiritists, shall certainly be put to death, they are to stone <dn>את</dn> them with stones. Their blood is upon them.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: The Set-Apartness of the Priests
readings.subtitle: Regulations for Mourning and Marriage
readings.text: [Leviticus 21:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>“Speak to the priests, the sons of Aharon, and say to them: ‘No one is to be defiled for the dead among his people,</dq> [2] <dq>except for his relatives who are nearest to him: for his mother, and for his father, and for his son, and for his daughter, and for his brother;</dq> [3] <dq>and for his maiden sister who is near to him, who has had no husband – for her he is defiled.</dq> [4] <dq>‘A leader does not defile himself among his people, to profane himself;</dq> [5] <dq>they do not make any bald place on their heads, and they do not shave the corner of their beard, and they do not make a cutting in their flesh.</dq> [6] <dq>‘They are set-apart to their <dn>Elohim</dn> and do not profane the Name of their <dn>Elohim</dn>, for they bring <dn>את</dn> the fire offerings of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and the bread of their <dn>Elohim</dn>, and shall be set-apart.</dq> [7] <dq>‘They do not take a woman who is a whore or a defiled woman, and they do not take a woman put away from her husband, for he is set-apart to his <dn>Elohim</dn>.</dq> [8] <dq>‘And you shall set him apart, for he brings <dn>את</dn> the bread of your <dn>Elohim</dn>, he is set-apart to you. For <dn>I</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, setting you apart, am set-apart.</dq> [9] <dq>‘And when the daughter of any priest profanes herself by whoring, she profanes <dn>את</dn> her father. She is burned with fire.</dq> [10] <dq>‘And the high priest among his brothers, on whose head the anointing oil was poured and who is ordained to wear the garments, does not unbind <dn>את</dn> his head nor tear his garments,</dq> [11] <dq>nor come near any dead body, nor defile himself for his father or his mother,</dq> [12] <dq>nor go out of the set-apart place, nor profane <dn>את</dn> the set-apart place of his <dn>Elohim</dn>, for the sign of dedication of the anointing oil of his <dn>Elohim</dn> is upon him. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [13] <dq>‘And let him take a wife in her maidenhood.</dq> [14] <dq>‘A widow or one put away or a defiled woman or a whore – <dn>את</dn> these he does not take. But a maiden of his own people he does take as a wife.</dq> [15] <dq>‘And he does not profane <dn>את</dn> his offspring among his people, for <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, who sets him apart.’ ”</dq> [16] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [17] <dq>“Speak to Aharon, saying, ‘No man of your offspring throughout their generations, who has any defect, is to draw near to bring the bread of his <dn>Elohim</dn>.</dq> [18] <dq>‘For any man who has a defect is not to draw near: a man blind or one lame or disfigured or deformed,</dq> [19] <dq>a man who has a broken foot or broken hand,</dq> [20] <dq>or is a hunchback or a dwarf, or a man who has a defect in his eye, or eczema or scab, or is a eunuch.</dq> [21] <dq>‘No man among the offspring of Aharon the priest, who has a defect, is to come near to bring <dn>את</dn> the offerings made by fire to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> – he has a defect, he does not come near to bring the bread of his <dn>Elohim</dn>.</dq> [22] <dq>‘He does eat the bread of his <dn>Elohim</dn>, both the most set-apart and the set-apart,</dq> [23] <dq>only, he does not go near the veil or approach the slaughter-place, because he has a defect, lest he profanes <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> set-apart places. For <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, who sets them apart.’ ”</dq> [24] Thus Mosheh spoke to Aharon and his sons, and to all the children of Yisra’ěl.

readings.title: Purity in Approaching the Offerings
readings.subtitle: Who May Eat the Set-Apart Food
readings.text: [Leviticus 22:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [2] <dq>“Speak to Aharon and his sons, that they separate themselves from the set-apart offerings of the children of Yisra’ěl, and that they do not profane <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> set-apart Name in what they set apart to <dn>Me</dn>. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [3] <dq>“Say to them, ‘Any man of all your offspring throughout your generations who draws near the set-apart offerings which the children of Yisra’ěl set apart to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, while he has uncleanness upon him, that being shall be cut off from before <dn>Me</dn>. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [4] <dq>‘Any man of the offspring of Aharon, who is a leper or has a discharge, does not eat the set-apart offerings until he is clean. And whoever touches what is rendered unclean by a being, or a man who has had an emission of semen,</dq> [5] <dq>or a man who touches any swarming creature by which he would be made unclean, or any being by whom he would become unclean, even any of his uncleanness;</dq> [6] <dq>the being who has touched it shall be unclean until evening, and does not eat the set-apart offerings, but shall bathe <dn>את</dn> his body in water.</dq> [7] <dq>‘And when the sun goes down he shall be clean, and afterward eat the set-apart offerings, because it is his food.</dq> [8] <dq>‘He does not eat that which dies or is torn by beasts, becoming unclean by it. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [9] <dq>‘And they shall guard <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> Charge, lest they bear sin for it and die thereby, when they profane it. <dn>I</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> set them apart.</dq> [10] <dq>‘And no stranger eats the set-apart offering. A sojourner with the priest, or a hired servant, does not eat the set-apart offering.</dq> [11] <dq>‘But when the priest buys a being with his silver, he does eat of it. And one who is born in his house does eat his food.</dq> [12] <dq>‘And when a priest’s daughter is married to a stranger, she does not eat of the set-apart offerings.</dq> [13] <dq>‘But when a priest’s daughter is a widow or put away, and has no child, and has returned to her father’s house as in her youth, she does eat her father’s food, but no stranger eats of it.</dq> [14] <dq>‘And when a man eats the set-apart offering by mistake, then he shall give <dn>את</dn> a set-apart offering to the priest, and add one-fifth to it.</dq> [15] <dq>‘And let the priests not profane <dn>את</dn> the set-apart offerings of the children of Yisra’ěl, which they lift up to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>,</dq> [16] <dq>or allow <dn>את</dn> them to bear the crookedness of trespass when they eat <dn>את</dn> their set-apart offerings. For <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, who sets them apart.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: Unblemished Sacrifices
readings.subtitle: Guarding the Commands of YeHoVaH
readings.text: [Leviticus 22:17] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [18] <dq>“Speak to Aharon and his sons, and to all the children of Yisra’ěl, and say to them, ‘Any man of the house of Yisra’ěl, or of the strangers in Yisra’ěl, who brings his offering for any of his vows or for any of his voluntary offerings, which they bring to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> as an ascending offering,</dq> [19] <dq>for your acceptance, is a male, a perfect one from the cattle, from the sheep, or from the goats.</dq> [20] <dq>‘Whatever has a defect, you do not bring, for it is not acceptable for you.</dq> [21] <dq>‘And when a man brings a slaughtering of peace offerings to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, to complete a vow, or a voluntary offering from the cattle or the sheep, it is to be perfect to be accepted, let there be no defect in it.</dq> [22] <dq>‘Those blind or broken or cut, or having an ulcer or eczema or scabs, you do not bring to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, nor make an offering by fire of them on the slaughter-place to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [23] <dq>‘As for a bull or a lamb that has any limb deformed or dwarfed you do prepare as a voluntary offering, but for a vow it is not accepted.</dq> [24] <dq>‘Do not bring to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> what is bruised or crushed, or torn or cut, nor do it in your land.</dq> [25] <dq>‘And from a son of a stranger’s hand you do not bring any of these as <dn>את</dn> the bread of your <dn>Elohim</dn>, for their corruption is in them, and defects are in them, they are not acceptable for you.’ ”</dq> [26] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [27] <dq>“When a bull or a sheep or a goat is born, it shall be seven days with its mother. And from the eighth day and thereafter it is acceptable as an offering made by fire to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [28] <dq>“But do not slay a cow or a sheep and <dn>את</dn> its young on the same day.</dq> [29] <dq>“And when you slaughter a slaughtering of thanksgiving to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, slaughter it for your acceptance.</dq> [30] <dq>“It is eaten that same day, leave none of it till morning. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [31] <dq>“And you shall guard <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> commands and do <dn>את</dn> them. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [32] <dq>“And do not profane <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> set-apart Name, and <dn>I</dn> shall be set-apart among the children of Yisra’ěl. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, who sets you apart,</dq> [33] <dq>who brought <dn>את</dn> you out of the land of Mitsrayim, to be your <dn>Elohim</dn>. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.”</dq>
